extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / 17th-century natural philosophers and experimentalists
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative and procedural criteria from a 17th-century Philosophical Transactions issue (mixed reports, observations, book notices and experimental queries) aimed at natural philosophers and experimental practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of painting (five)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those principles of art constantly observed by the ancients in their works, are here enumerated to be five: 1. Invention or the history. 2. Proportion or symmetry. 3. Colour (wherein is also contained the just dispensation of the lights and shades). 4. Motion, in which are expressed the actions and passions. 5. The regular position of the figures of the whole work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invention and expression are more spiritual and refined; the proportion, colouring, and perspective, the more mechanical part of this art. The principles are drawn from observations made by Pliny and Quintilian upon celebrated ancient painters and paralleled with famous modern painters (Leonardo, Raphael, Julio Romano, N. Poussin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antimony veterinary dosage and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner of using it is this: Take one dram of crude antimony powdered for one horse, and when you give him his oats in the morning, shake it upon his oats in a little heap in the middle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the horse is hungry and the head is kept off other parts of the oats, he will snap it up; some horses like it, others refuse after the first — if so cover it with oats thinly or make it into balls. Anecdotal efficacy claims: fattening pigs and horses, curing measles in pigs, curing farcins in a horse after one week. (Context: presented as an observing person's report.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for producing insect-based dyes (cochineal alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: dry and/or stamp herbs/berries/woods, infuse or boil to extract tincture, evaporate to a thick syrup, place the mass in an earthen/wooden vessel covered with straw and placed in a shady pit/ditch with wet leaves or putrifying matter around; allow fermentation so that first a 'shelly husky worm' and then a fly of the tincture are produced; collect flies from the sides/surface of the vessel, kill in a warm pan or stove, dry and keep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied both to herbs/berries and pulverized woods (infuse, boil, evaporate to consistency). For berries: stamp and boil to a 'rob' and then treat similarly. The author suggests this could produce a durable dye as good as cochineal. Editorial note: 'The whole tenor of this inaccurate and ill-written paper betrays great ignorance respecting the generation of insects. The coccus insect is not engendered by the juice of the cactus plant, but is merely nourished by it.' — caution: the biological premises are incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental queries for vegetation (research questions and trial suggestions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of direct experimental questions to investigate plant growth and sap movement: e.g., which vegetables will grow when set with 'wrong end' downward; whether branches laid to root while on tree and then cut will shoot forward/backward; in tapping/cutting/boring whether juice comes from above or below; which part of bark ascends/descends sap; effects of cutting a two- or three-inch zone of bark on a branch; use and role of pith and whether juice ascends/descends by it; effects of boring trunk to pith and driving pegs; whether cutting root ends causes copious bleeding; what side/age of tree yields most sap; best seasons/time-of-day for sap yield; effects of rain amount on sap; whether tree nature can be changed by applying juices to roots; whether roots covered from rain but branches exposed will grow; whether inoculated roots will grow; how short root arms can be cut and still survive; how deep to plant different trees; whether seeds planted either way will grow equally; whether a stem set with root turned up will grow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many of these are phrased as direct experimental trials ('This to be tried in the most pithy plants'), suggesting hands-on manipulations (cutting zones, boring to pith, pegging holes, inoculating roots) and systematic observation over seasons/times to answer functional and physiological questions about sap movement, rooting, and propagation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive hypothesis must be testable and verifiable by observation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hypothesis (here: the doctrine of the magnet and variations of the magnetic needle) produces predictions (a table of predicted variations by year), it is published so 'that inquisitive men may every where from time to time make observations accordingly, either to verify or invalidate the proposed theory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author provides a concrete table of predicted magnetic variation values for many years and explicitly frames the prediction as a public, testable claim inviting repeated observation to confirm or refute it — a standard for scientific hypotheses: produce falsifiable, verifiable predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content checklist for a comprehensive comet treatise (cometography)
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough comet work should explain the whole nature of comets: their place, parallaxes, distances from the earth, beginning and end, the several appearances of their heads and trains, with their admirable motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He illustrates that such a work should rest on a constant hypothesis (e.g., motion in a straight line and generation from vapours issuing from the sun and planets) and include schemes/figures and historical explication of notable comets; recommended additions include tables summarizing times of first apparition, duration, place, motion (direct/retrograde), speed, size/figure/colour of heads, and magnitude/shape/position of tails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics for a gauging (stereometry) treatise
rubrics_metrics.description: A stereometrical treatise intended for gauging should include measurement methods for all kinds of solids generated by rotations of circles and conic sections — spheres, spheroids, conoids, spindles, and their segments, zones, ungulas, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work cited (Robert Anderson) is an 'elaborate treatise' on these solids, implying comprehensive formulae/derivations and applicability to practical gauging problems (e.g., measurement of volumes for trade/industry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn-lath polishing method for optical glasses
rubrics_metrics.description: An artist at Paris polishes optic-glasses on a turn-lath with the same ease as he turns wood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a production technique for telescope lenses; the text also mentions an extraordinary burning-glass at Milan (seven feet diameter) claimed to burn at ~33 feet — evidence of novel instrumentation and manufacturing approaches worth noting and (implicitly) replicating/assessing.
